purpose: This table holds individual commercial flight records departing New York-area airports (EWR, JFK, LGA) during the first half of 2013, combining flight schedule and performance data (carrier, flight number, scheduled and actual departure/arrival times, delays, cancellation status) with reference attributes about the operating aircraft and the origin and destination airports.
usage: Read the table at the grain of one row per flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, and origin_airport combination, representing a single scheduled flight leg. Use the delay and timing fields (dep_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_hhmm, arr_delay_minutes, air_time_minutes) to analyze on-time performance, noting these are null for flights that did not depart or complete. Aircraft attribute columns and destination reference columns are null when the source tail number or destination airport did not match the corresponding reference data.
limitations: The profile could not confirm a unique tail-number-per-flight relationship because tail_number carries a 0.9% null_rate (1521 nulls) and cannot serve as a grain key; the proposed grain (flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, origin_airport) is unverified until measured against the warehouse. Aircraft attribute columns are null for roughly 16-18% of rows, and destination reference columns are null for about 2.1% of rows, both consistent with unmatched reference lookups rather than data entry omissions, but the profile cannot confirm the cause. captured_at appears to be a pipeline ingestion timestamp (16 distinct values within a 16-second window in 2026) despite not being flagged as airbyte metadata in the profile; reviewers should confirm whether it should be governed as metadata. sched_dep_hour_local and sched_dep_minute_local appear derivable from sched_dep_hhmm; the profile cannot confirm whether they are redundant or carry independent meaning.
